keyVerseText: Making request, if by any means now at length I might have a prosperous journey by the will of God to come unto you.
rootMeaning: The word εὐοδόω (euodóō) is derived from the compound of εὖ (eû), meaning 'good' or 'well,' and ὁδός, meaning 'way' or 'road.' This etymology conveys the literal sense of 'to have a good or successful journey.' Beyond the common English gloss of 'prosper' or 'succeed,' the root meaning emphasizes the assistance and favorable conditions experienced along a path or journey, whether physical or metaphorical.
usageInScripture: In Scripture, εὐοδόω appears four times and is consistently translated with the idea of prospering or having a successful journey. The top translations include 'mayest prosper' (twice), 'I might have a prosperous journey' (once), and 'God hath prospered him' (once). This range shows the word's application both to physical journeys and to broader success, such as in business or personal affairs, highlighting its versatile use in expressing divine favor and effective progress.
theologicalSignificance: Theologically, εὐοδόω underscores God's providential care and blessing over the believer's path, whether literal travel or life's endeavors. It reflects the biblical truth that success and prosperity are not merely human achievements but are granted by God's will and help. This word invites believers to trust in God's guidance and to seek His will for their journeys, recognizing that true prosperity is rooted in divine approval and assistance. It also encourages a posture of dependence on God for fruitful outcomes in all aspects of life.
keyVerseReflection: Romans 1:10 says, 'Making request, if by any means now at length I might have a prosperous journey by the will of God to come unto you.' Here, εὐοδόω conveys more than just a safe trip; it expresses a deep desire for God's sovereign blessing and timing in Paul's travel. The word enriches the verse by highlighting that the success of Paul's journey is contingent upon God's gracious will, reinforcing the theme of divine sovereignty and the believer's reliance on God for all endeavors.
